description:
FOUND s502 (Fable, 2026-09-30) by the s501 review probe `r500a-proto.pl` (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s501/review/): its `parse` row's fourth field `scalar(my @x = LIST)` reads 1 where perl reads 2 -- and it reads 1 on the BASE (77212b1f) and on 558cc5a0 too: PRE-EXISTING, not an s500a mover (NOTES.md called the row "right today", which was true only of its first three fields).

REPRODUCER (scratchpad lc2.pl; perl 5.40.3 first, PCL main c0edaf75 second):
    use constant LIST => (1, 2); use constant NAMES => qw(a b c);
    my @f = LIST; print "f @f | ", scalar(@f), "\n";      # perl: f 1 2 | 2      PCL: f 2 | 1
    my @n = NAMES; print "n @n | ", scalar(@n), "\n";     # perl: n a b c | 3    PCL: n c | 1
    print "direct ", join(",", LIST), " ", join(",", NAMES), "\n";   # perl: 1,2 a,b,c   PCL: 2 c
    my @m = (LIST, 3); print "m @m\n";                    # perl: m 1 2 3        PCL: m 2 3
    for my $x (NAMES) { print "it $x\n" }                 # perl: 3 lines        PCL: one line, "it c"
    print "cnt ", scalar(() = NAMES), "\n";               # perl: cnt 3          PCL: cnt 1
    print "idx ", (NAMES)[1], "\n";                       # perl: idx b          PCL: idx (empty)
Scalar context (perl's constant.pm installs `sub () { @list }` for a multi-value constant, so scalar context is the COUNT): `my $s = L; scalar(L)` -> perl 3 / PCL 3 by accident (last element == count for (1,2,3)); `scalar(Q)` for `qw(a b)` -> perl 2, PCL "b". A ONE-value constant and the empty `=> ()` constant are right today (`d 1`, `e 0` in scratchpad lc.pl).

MECHANISM (the emission, `./pl2cl`): the constant sub is printed WITHOUT the wantarray dispatch every other list-returning sub gets --
    sub two { (7, 8) }          -> (p-sub pl-two (&rest %_args) (...) (p-args-body (block nil (if *wantarray* (vector 7 8) (progn 7 8)))))
    use constant L => (1, 2)    -> (p-sub pl-L (&rest %_args) () (progn %_args (progn 1 2)))
so the body is a plain `progn` of the values and the caller receives the last one. The site is Pl/Parser.pm `_process_constant` (single form, ~line 11151: `my $cl_value = $self->_compile_constant_value($value_parts);` then the p-sub print at ~11154) -- `_compile_constant_value` compiles the value list through ExprToCL as an expression (a comma list -> progn). The hash form `use constant { A => 1 }` cannot carry a list (perl forbids it) so only the single form is affected.

FIX SHAPE (rule 11 -- the sibling is the ordinary sub body): when the value has more than one top-level comma element, emit the body in the same shape as a normal sub returning a literal list -- `(if *wantarray* (vector V1 V2 ...) N)` where N = the element COUNT (perl: `sub () { @list }`, so scalar context is the count, NOT the last element -- probed above) -- or route the value through the same `p-args-body`/wantarray lowering `sub NAME () { (V1, V2) }` would take, whichever is the one existing path. The `()` prototype registration (#2533's `:prototype ""` fact, `register_constant_prototype`) stays: perl's list constants ARE `()`-prototyped, so `L + 1` still parses as a term. Note that a list constant's elements may be expressions (`use constant DIRS => ("$ENV{HOME}/a", "$ENV{HOME}/b")`) evaluated ONCE at `use` time -- perl evaluates `@list` at BEGIN; today's emission re-evaluates the body per call, which is the same for both shapes and is a separate, older question (leave it).

POPULATION: 0 of the everyday corpus, 1 perl-tests file (tr.t), 0 cpan-tests/modules, 0 of repo lib/ -- but **18 files of perl's core lib** that PCL loads from the perlbrew tree: IO/Socket/IP.pm, IO/Compress/Zip/Constants.pm, IO/Compress/Gzip/Constants.pm, Fatal.pm, IPC/Cmd.pm, App/Prove.pm, App/Prove/State.pm, Archive/Tar/Constant.pm, File/Fetch.pm, ExtUtils/Constant/{Utils,Base}.pm, constant.pm itself, + 6 more (`grep -rlE 'use constant\s+\w+\s*=>\s*(\(|qw)' ~/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3/`). Any program that loads one of those and reads such a constant is silently wrong today.

BARS when fixed: emission change -> generation bump + the three artifacts regenerated; `tools/corpus-diff.pl` (tr.t and every file with a list constant will differ -- explain by class); the full sweep; guard rows = the reproducer above (all eight lines + the scalar-context COUNT row for qw(a b)) in an existing Pl/t file whose wall time allows, inverse-verified on a base extraction. Probe the BREAKING case: a one-value constant whose value is a parenthesised expression `use constant X => (1 + 2)` must stay a scalar 3, and `use constant E => ()` must stay empty (perl: `my @e = E` is 0 elements; `scalar(E)` is 0).

Sibling finding filed alongside: #2538 (Scalar::Util::set_prototype is an empty stub).


=== s501b (2026-09-30): a perl-suite file depends on this ===
t/op/sigsystem.t declares `use constant TRUE => ($^X, '-e', 'exit 0')` and calls `system(TRUE)` twenty times.  Under PCL TRUE returns only "exit 0", so the call is `system("exit 0")`.  Before s501b's #2082 that one string went to /bin/sh and exited 0 -- two ACCIDENTAL passes; with perl's one-string rule (no metacharacter -> split and execvp) it answers -1, exactly what perl answers for `system("exit 0")`.  The file moved OK 4/0 -> DIFF 2/2 and its two rows ("system() without/with reaper succeeded 10 times out of 10") now cite this task in baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv: fixing the list constant should bring op/sigsystem.t back to 4/0 (re-run it and edit the two rows out).

=== DONE (s502e, Opus, 2026-10-04) ===
SHIPPED: Pl/Parser.pm `_compile_constant_value` + `_constant_list_arity` -- a value that is a comma list of two or more top-level elements (seen through single-child paren layers) is compiled in LIST context; the constant body is `(let ((%const-list VEC)) (if *wantarray* %const-list (length %const-list)))` -- perl's `sub () { @list }`.  Single values, `(1 + 2)`, `qw(z)` and `()` keep the scalar body.  Normative: docs/ir-spec.md (the `:prototype` facts note, "A list-valued use constant").
PROBES (scratch/s502e/p/lc.pl 22 rows, lc2.pl 8 rows): == perl incl. the breaking cases ((1+2) is 3, E => () empty / scalar undef, qw(z), ONE + 1, NAMES + 1 = 4 (count + 1), prototype ''), a package-qualified constant, BEGIN, map, (L)[-1], [L], nested paren list, a call inside the list; the base differs on every list row.  Core modules: Archive::Tar::Constant / IO::Compress::{Zip,Gzip}::Constants load and read identically before/after (most of the "18 files" hits were single parenthesised values; IPC::Cmd's SPECIAL_CHARS is the one real list constant, and IPC::Cmd / IO::Socket::IP do not load under PCL at all on the base either -- Module::Metadata transpile / Socket getaddrinfo, pre-existing).
COMPANION: op/sigsystem.t DIFF 2/2 -> OK 4/0, its two #2537 rows edited out of baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv and the snapshot row edited.
GUARD: Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t rows 75-76 (inverse-verified failing on e5d72352 and 618db500 extractions).
corpus-diff: no list constant in the 111-file corpus (identical at the member's commit).


=== s502e resume (s507, claude-opus-5-5) ===
Scope, said plainly: #2537 covers a COMMA LIST or qw() of >= 2 elements as the constant value. Residue found by Fable s507 review probe e1-const: #2680 (an EMPTY constant is one undef element in a list -- the general empty-sub bug, rows 04/44) and #2681 (a SINGLE list-yielding expression, `1 .. 5` / `map {...}`, is still compiled in scalar context; the value is re-evaluated at every use, rows 31/32). Not widened here.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a LIST-valued `use constant` (`use constant L => (1, 2)`, `=> qw(a b c)`) returns ONLY ITS LAST ELEMENT -- `my @f = L` is (2), `for my $x (NAMES)` iterates once, `join(",", L)` is "2", `(L)[1]` is empty; perl gives the whole list (and its COUNT in scalar context)
